newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia says ties with Israel on hold.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia says ties with Israel on hold.

text.p: Tunisia has put relations with Israel on hold because its right-wing government has failed to honour agreements signed with the Palestinians, Tunisian Foreign Minister Habib Ben Yahia told parliament on Monday night.
"Several of you have asked for a break for reflection over normalisation with Israel. This is exactly the state of Tunisian-Israeli relations," the minister said.
Tunisia and Israel formally established low-level diplomatic relations this year by opening offices in Tunis and Tel Aviv. Tunisia also opened a mission in the Palestinian-administered Gaza Strip.
"The new Israeli government has gone back on Israel's commitments and rejected the implementation of agreements signed with the Palestinian Authority," Ben Yahia said.
"Its acts and expansion of settlements are continuing in violation of acccords and international decisions," he added.
"We must stand seriously and firmly against that in a way that safeguards Palestinian rights and peace in the region based on the land for peace formula," Ben Yahia said.
Under a peace accord with the PLO, Israel was due to to have redeployed its troops by the end of last March in Hebron, the last major Arab West Bank city still under Israeli control.
The government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who took office in June, has also lifted a freeze on building new settlements imposed by the previous Labour government.
